subject: Re: EastUS3 latency + 5xx burst — failover request & exec update
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcare.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Ramirez <sre@apexcare.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: EastUS3: sudden 5xx + p99 latency spike — immediate help needed

Nikhil / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors and p99 latency from ~09:05 PT in EastUS3. Error rate jumped from ~0.1% to 6.8% and p99 latency moved from ~380ms to ~3.2s. This is affecting checkout flows for a subset of customers (ApexCare EU & US patients).

Attached: sample logs and a short CSV of the last 30 minutes of traffic. On-call (Diego) is copied.

Can you confirm whether we can fail traffic to EastUS2 as an immediate mitigation? We need an ETA for failover and any impact on session affinity/data residency we should communicate to product.

Lena
Engineering Manager, ApexCare

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EastUS3: sudden 5xx + p99 latency spike — immediate help needed

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — we see the same signal on our end (alerts fired at 09:06).

Immediate plan:
- I’m standing up a regional incident bridge and tagging this P0.
- Requesting permission to initiate a geo-redispatch (EastUS3 -> EastUS2) as a mitigant while we investigate root cause.
- Marissa (SRE) will lead the traffic steering + circuit-breaker work; Vanessa will coordinate customer comms.

Questions for you: any strict session affinity requirements for the affected endpoints? Also confirm whether downstream systems (payment gateways) can tolerate cross-region reads for the short window.

I’ll update in 15 and post the bridge link.

—Nikhil
Sr. Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcare.com>, Diego Ramirez <sre@apexcare.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Recommended action: geo-redispatch + model-fraction downgrade

Team — quick internal summary and recommendation (saved playbook: geo-redispatch-playbook.pdf attached):

Findings so far:
- Spike localized to EastUS3 serving cluster; kernel-level telemetry shows elevated GPU queuing and sustained KV cache contention.
- Errors are predominantly 502/504 with a smaller share of model OOMs on long-context endpoints.

Recommended mitigations (rollout):
1) Immediate: enable circuit-breaker & prefix-KV cache bypass for EastUS3 traffic, then initiate controlled geo-redispatch to EastUS2 at 60% traffic for affected routes.
2) Short term: switch affected model variant to the quantized-8bit profile (same family) to reduce memory pressure; maintain graded rollout to avoid sudden capacity spikes.
3) Monitoring: roll forward metrics dashboard and enable aggressive alerting on p50/p95/p99 and 5xx rate; we keep the bridge open.

Risk & exec ask:
- Cross-region routing will incur ~12–15s session reconnection for live sessions; some in-flight requests may error — we will issue a customer notice.
- Need executive sign-off for cross-region steering (data residency exception) and approval to apply a 1% service credit for impacted customers if the failover window exceeds 90 minutes.

I’m starting the traffic steering now pending confirmation. Attachments: geo-redispatch-playbook.pdf.

Marissa
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: geo-redispatch-playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 260KB)]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcare.com>

Subject: Re: EastUS3: sudden 5xx + p99 latency spike — immediate help needed

Thanks, team. We authorize the controlled geo-redispatch to EastUS2. ApexCare legal has a standing clause for transient cross-region routing for incident mitigation — Diego confirms.

Please provide an ETA for:
- initial traffic shift start
- expected time to observe p99 < 800ms and 5xx < 0.5%

We’ll prepare a short customer note once the first metrics look stable.

Lena

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Executive Distribution <execs@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcare.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: EastUS3 incident — post-mitigation exec summary and follow-ups

EXEC SUMMARY (final):
- Timeline: alerts at 09:06 PT; geo-redispatch initiated 09:41 PT (60% traffic); full ramp to 95% by 10:03 PT.
- Impact: p99 reduced from ~3.2s -> 540ms within 18 minutes of initial shift; 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.3% by 10:12 PT.
- Root cause (preliminary): sustained KV cache eviction storm + queuing on EastUS3 serving nodes under mixed-length traffic. We observed elevated memory churn on two host groups; investigating scheduler/kernel scheduling regressions.

Actions taken:
- Controlled geo-redispatch to EastUS2, temporary model-fraction downgrade to quantized-8bit for affected routes, applied circuit-breaker tuning and additional capacity in EastUS3.
- Customer comms: ApexCare on-call acknowledged and will notify their enterprise customers.
- Post-incident: we have opened INF-4821 for the kernel-level regression and assigned a 72-hour remediation SLA for a mitigation patch.

Open items / asks:
- Exec approval to proceed with a rolling kernel patch in EastUS3 outside standard maintenance window (risk: short-term pod restarts). Recommended window: tonight 00:30–02:30 PT.
- Approve the proposed customer goodwill: 1% service credit to impacted customers if outage window (for a given tenant) exceeded 90 minutes. Legal & finance to finalize amount.

Metrics & attachments: see attached traffic CSV and playbook used during the operation.

I’ll coordinate the postmortem and timeline for the mitigation patch. Thanks to the SRE/serving teams for the rapid response.

—Nikhil Sharma
Sr. Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
